item.title: Re: The Sanctum
item.content:encoded:
Thx for the feedback it's really helpful and appreciated.

In terms of how the Sanctum has remained hidden, it's because they acted in secrecy on par with the foundation, the Star of Bethlehem (SOB) guiding them to anomalies before the foundation can get to them. Another main reason is because of the heavy self-isolation the Sanctum has, it didn't know the foundation existed. It wasn't until the foundation became fully efficient that they were able to track and find anomalies just as fast as the Sanctum and the two eventually clashed leading to the vanishing agents, and later the Sanctum's discovery.

In terms of relations with other GoI, the Sanctum worked in heavy secrecy and mainly operated inside of Italy and Europe so its existence is almost unknown to the whole world aside from the Foundation when it's uncovered. But the foundation does find members of the Serpent's Hand contained within the prison, but the Serpent's hand are unaware of who was responsible.

SCP-914 is an older writing (from series 1), and primarily since a lot of nostalgia surrounds it, it's less likely to be edited.

Try to read some newer SCP's and see if there's any difference, as newer entries tend to have a different feel to them. They may be written with less common language.

item.title: (SEEKING GREENLIGHT) This Number is no Longer in Service
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional

Page Layout: I plan to use the traditional SCP format with an ACS header. The plot will reveal itself through the recovery log and a set of phone calls received by the object.

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: In the 1968 the Foundation incepted a package from one of their mailrooms. The package contained a 1940’s rotary dial telephone that receives a phone call every day at 12:00 AM despite the cord being cut. The same phone call is repeated nightly until it is changed by the caller. The phone calls slowly reveal the story of a foundation researcher who has been captured by the Chaos Insurgency. He intended to send the phone to his family in hopes to ensure them that he is safe.

Central Narrative: The calls the man makes to his family slowly reveal a story. In the first call he will inform his family that “the guys at work” have a job for him and that he won’t be home for a little while. In the second phone call the man is less optimistic, however his tone is still hopeful and he attempts to ensure his wife that he will be home soon. He refers to his captures as “they”. In the final phone calls he refers to his captures as the Insurgency (Chaos Insurgency) and is mostly pessimistic in tone. In the final phone call, he apologizes to his family and is ill. These phone calls will take place over the course of 50 years.

An addendum at the end of the article will state that the foundation visited the home address that the man sent the package to. House was empty and it is implied that the family living there was killed by the Chaos Insurgency. This is meant to get an emotional response out of the reader. Not only were his calls not received by his family, but rather the foundation, but his family may not have been alive this entire time.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This article will stand out because of its extremely simple concept that requires emotional investment. It is easy for any reader to understand (you do not even need to know what the Chaos Insurgency is to understand the basic premise). It is meant to be a refreshing break from the more complex articles on the site.

Additional Notes: The following information will be given during the article:
1. No phone calls can be made on the phone. It functions as a normal, disconnected phone when not receiving its nightly call.
2. The object is classified as neutralized, as it no longer makes calls.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Doctor Juhan! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

YouTube is quite the introduction power to the SCP Universe it seems! It's awesome to see you decided to join our ~official site~ after being a fan for quite a time - you'd be surprised at how many people don't do that and just stay in the shadows.

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we?

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Re: Architecture of sites and areas
item.content:encoded:
My headcanon is that you might have a lobby where the place looks a little better or a major campus-type site might have a fancy front office building for impressing politicians or representatives, but outside that sites are designed by engineers, not architects.

That is, the office and light lab areas have that look where you can swap hallways between any generic office, academic campus, research facility, government building or hospital by changing the colors of the walls and tile. You can furnish your office, cubicle, and/or quarters as you like (within reason), and there's obviously going to be human touches like plants in empty corners and parrot streamers left up in the lounge from last year's luau-themed staff cookout, but for the structure itself, the key word is "pragmatic". Cubicle farms and copy-paste design are the rule, and you wouldn't see much difference between low-security humanoid containment cells and quarters for resident staff.

Hardened lab and high security areas drop even that much accommodation to comfort-
+ and are where the concept-development side of my brain really kicks in.
- Cue Danny Elfman Music:

The standard architecture for a mass storage site is a three dimensional grid of reinforced columns, bulkheads, and crossmembers, spaced with redundant support capacity in expectation that sooner or later something is going breach and take a bunch of them with it. Concrete, refractory brick, and powder-painted steel are the materials of choice; convoluted networks of pipes and cables line the walls and ceilings. These areas tend to be underground with floorspace most relatably measured in city blocks.

Need a few humanoid containment chambers? Fill in a cube of support columns, add subdivisions, doors and catwalks as needed. Need a bigger room? Tear down a wall or two, annex a section of hallway.

Sites of this sort almost inevitably become winding mazes of hallways threaded between chambers, with near constant construction and reconstruction going on as new anomalies are contained and the needs of existing ones shift. Following pipes marked with yellow triangles or green "5"s is often the most reliable means of navigation, and periodic reviews are done to separate genuine reports of structural anomalies from hallways that disappeared due to renovation.

item.title: The Knife (SEEKING GREENLIGHT)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Elevator Pitch: It's a kitchen knife with coordinates on it leading to a small island which doesn't seem to have any anomalous activity. If anyone lays an eye on the knife, without a camera or artist depiction, they will hear whispers of voices telling them to 'become one with him'. The Foundation currently does not know what this phrase means. Anyways, the victim will have an urge to equip the knife to once again 'become one with him'. The victim will chant 'I must become one with him' and once said victim holds up the knife, the victim is now considered a 'host'. The host will be controlled by some unknown entity and is severely hostile to humans. After host manages to catch an unfortunate being, it will ingest the victim before falling dead and the knife will dematerialize and then materialize in a random location. Witnesses who manage to get a glimpse of the host will suddenly suffer cardiac arrest due to unknown means. Cameras or artist depictions do not trigger the knife's affects.

Central Narrative: Several reports came through on an evening saying that multiple civilians have mysteriously gone 'insane' and a another bunch have somehow created a cult around a specific kitchen knife worshipping it. Then other reports came in reporting that multiple civilians in a town began acting strange and soon enough the entire town was in anarchy. Eventually, the Foundation found out about this strange event and so 'invaded' the town, securing it and the knife with the loss of 7 agents in the process. The remaining agents all suddenly chanted 'This world will fall into anarchy' after the mission.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It includes a mysterious 'him' which could make the reader figure out who this 'him' was and why the cult was created along with why the chanting occurs.

Additional Notes: First attempt at making my own SCP sooo.. yeah it probably won't be that good but eh

item.title: Feedbacker/Infinite Repeater
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Black Comedy

Page Layout: Basic Entry w/ interview logs

Elevator Pitch: Stoner musician buys a Delay pedal from UK antique shop, and upon maxing out the "feedback" knob, the pedal infinitely loops what he last played, even when all power is disconnected. The feedback loop eventually enters his head and weirdness ensues.

Central Narrative: Jason Higgs purchases a cheap BOSS DD-3 delay pedal from his local antiques shop (town of Rye, Sussex, UK). He takes it home, and inhales a cosmic bong rip before maxing out all the pedals' settings to create a "wavey soundscape". Upon turning off his amplifier, he is surprised to find the sound of the feedback loop continuing.

After disconnecting his amp and pedal of power, the loop continues still, and his panic gradually intensifies. After a few days he attemps to destroy the pedal, but after throwing it against a concrete wall he is struck with what he later describes as a stroke. He awakens minutes later, find the pedal still perfectly intact. He throws it into a nearby bush in panic, and begins pacing toward the hospital a few miles away. To his horror, he begins hearing the same feedback loop in his head, although faintly.

He arrives at the hospitals' A&E ward, and in short he is eventually transfered to another hospitals' psych ward following his manic behaviour. The staff of both hospitals found nothing medically wrong with him, and found no quantifiable evidence of a "feedback loop in his head".

2 weeks later, he tells the doctors that the loop has "syncronised" with his heartbeat, and that it has gradually grown louder and lowered in pitch. It is at this point he learns he is being held at an SCP site in Kent. He is interviewed orally (albeit unsuccesfully as the loop has nearly completely inhibited his hearing) then interviewed via text communication.

Another week later, he claims the loop has gotten so low in pitch that it's like an earthquake inside of him, thrumming with every pulse of his heart (which is now beating around 12BPM). He begs to die, and eventually is terminated after the foundation fail to extract any new information from him.

While all this has been going on, the foundation recover the item itself (after Jason tells them where he discarded it) and run a number of tests on it. They test the effects of the item on several D-Class, who all respond similarly to Jason although with slight variations depending on test subjects' mental fortitude. It seems to take around 5-7 days from first hearing it for the loop to "enter" the subjects' mind, although it seems this process was accelerated for Jason when he attempted to destroy it.

They attempt to break into the item (which strangely contains no serial number or text on the back as is usual of BOSS products) using several implements and methods (hammer, diamond drill, industrial press) but with no success.

The item has a way of disabling or nulifying any violent force applied to it, and shows only slight superficial stratches when dropped from great heights or launched long distances. It is also extremely heat resistant, and is not corroded by strong acids. It is then contained in a glass display case in a small 3mx3m room, and classified as "Safe".

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Mysterious but recognisable item with strange anomalous "effect", music related, largely unexplained

Additional Notes: Hope this isn't too long! Let me know if so and i'll try to be more concise on my next go round. Most may not get this, but BOSS pedals are known for being extremely sturdy and well made anyway, so it's kind of a joke that it's indestructable. I tried to make it interesting without this knowledge, however :)

Forum thread: Feedbacker/Infinite Repeater

item.title: Re: Awaiting Greenlight / The Book of the Siners
item.content:encoded:
Hmmmm the problem I had before and the problem I have with a lot of first timers is that they end up giving a vague summary of/or a vague series of events and call it a narrative. While your updated pitch certainly is significantly improved, it still falls under very vague and not developed.

Maybe I can think of an example to help show you. Since you're doing something very biblical, I'll use God's creation of Adam and Eve as an example.

+I'll just add this example...
-Yeet

Imagine if the Garden of Eden and the creation of Adam and Eve and existence was someone's pitch. A lot of newbies would make something like this:

  • Powerful being creates everything

I'd ask for expansion and they'd do something along the lines of:

  • Powerful being makes universe, makes a garden and puts life in garden

When I want in-depth expansion. Not just a short summary replaced with a different, slightly more focused short vague summary.

What I want is:

  • An omnipotent, powerful being takes seven days to create all forms of life and locates them in the Garden of Eden. He creates Adam and allows him to enjoy the garden. He then creates Eve to be his companion. One day, a snake tempts them with the fruit of knowledge and God casts them out of the Garden, starting off the human race as we know it.

See what I mean? All three kinda mean the same thing (God creates everything) but the third one is the most interesting.

Your current one falls in a weird area slightly past the second example I have and way short of the third. I understand my example definitely isn't a perfect example, but I hope I helped elaborate on what I was looking for.

Now, I know this may disappoint, but I almost always only take two looks at any concept or draft. I'll be declining to return any more now. You can seek out other reviewers via the butterfly squad roster. They're really good people, so don't be shy now. If any of them don't respond in a few days, you can always send followup PMs as long as you're not spamming them. Keep in mind if a reviewer is in high demand and has a busy personal life, there's a possibility they can gloss over you by mistake. They're not ignoring you, they're just busy people. Don't sweat it.

You're definitely getting there, so don't give up! The greenlight process can be a challenging one, but the end result is well, well worth it. Have a good day, partner.

P.S. I'm not exactly a high demand reviewer, so thank you for reaching out to me and considering me 👍 it felt nice

I want to use this to show how he thinks hes at war at them and has an entire site going to to study and research, but no one else in the entire dimension cares or notices. I'm trying to create the sense of isolation, even in varied and unique company. As for his death, I'm trying to contrast the end of the journal as his crazed ravings are abruptly cut short by something very mundane, and even though he sees himself as a pioneer and his own site manager, he just trips over and falls down a small cliff, ending everything. He will then soberly read over his journal again and reflect on what he does, but not realising what happened to him and seriously believing he was a hero. I hope this makes sense to you.

item.title: Forum Crit Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: The Sanctum
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: GoI format/Potential for separate SCP article on the prison and the Star of Bethlehem.

Genre (Optional): History, Horror, Action

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP article. Numerous addendums and field reports/logs as the foundation push deeper into the prison.

Elevator Pitch: Numerous SCPs undocumented by the foundation is located in the most unlikely place, The Vatican City. Beneath the city lies a 300-meter deep prison protected by powerful Templars, and priests known as Arminda's. The ancient prison contains SCPs via 'blessings' granted by the 'Star of Bethlehem' a large light orb at the top of the prison, which in itself is it's own SCP.

Central Narrative: The story begins when foundation agents in Italy begin to vanish, and once found are clueless on their allegiance to the foundation, appearing to not remember the foundation at all. The investigation leads the foundation to the Vatican City, with numerous unknown agents responsible for the agent's state being linked to there.

+ Further Narrative
- Title for hiding text

To understand the cause of this, the foundation sent in an infiltration unit into the Vatican to watch for bizarre activity, having a live feed and wiretaps attached to them. Upon entering, the squad found nothing out of the ordinary, until they witnessed a singular man in white robes wall through a large display waterfall and vanish. The foundation now had proof that anomalous activity was occurring within the Vatican, and would have surely been able to uncover more there and then if the squad had returned…

Concerned for a potential hostile threat, the SCP foundation conducted a full investigation into the activity. Including a squad sent to contain the white-robed priest- but yet again the squad failed to return, no bodies, no trace. Eventually, the foundation launched a full raid on the Vatican, and what they would uncover was The Sanctum, the Vatican's very own version of the SCP Foundation, home to over 300 undocumented SCPs. In the center was a large pit traveling down 300 meters, and above was a bright ball of light that appeared to light the whole prison.

Upon entering, the foundation made contact with those who ran this facility. Ancient knights known as the Templars, and white-robed priests known as Armindas. When met, a man in a golden robe told the strike team "Welcome to The Sanctum, but this is no place for you." Attempting to force entry brought hostility, and a fight broke out between the strike team and The Templars, who despite wielding only armor, swords, and shields, were able to dispatch enough foundation units to force a retreat. From this point, The Sanctum is declared an enemy of The Foundation, and a full platoon of mobile task for units are sent in to claim the facility, but they fail, the mysterious orb of light beginning to vaporize the units as they descend to the bottom.

The story continues as the foundation attempts to decide whether to take the Sanctum by force or attempt to negotiate and uncover the true power of the orb of light what the Sanctum call 'The Star of Bethlehem' and why and how they contain anomalies. But most importantly, what lurks at the very bottom of the prison. (There is a bit more to fit in but I didn't want to cram this article, but if you wish to hear more do ask!)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I believe the idea has a lot of potentials to introduce new things the foundation never knew existed and uncover the true power that the Sanctum holds, and how it and the Foundation tetters on war or peace with each other. And the secret of what lies at the bottom of the prison, along with finding out how and why the Sanctum does such things.

Additional Notes: N/A

item.title: Re: Foundation 2.0
item.content:encoded:
Interesting SCP you've got there!
Would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

Oooooh! Parrallel Dimensions? Sign me the heck up!
I'll be honest: I fricking love this idea. Trapped in a parallel world? The place you worked and loved and served for so long in ruins? Present in a place with no resemblance to your own world? No wonder he'd go insane! Oh, and the journal? Pure gold. I love it.
Although I do have a few concerns/suggestions:

  • Having him die in the end seems a bit out-of-place. Maybe have a series of transmissions he attempts to send to the foundation be the the last communication received from him? Leaving his actual ending ambiguous? Or maybe have him be hunted to death by the villagers?
  • The method used for teleportation is quite clever, although the entry of 507 and the guard into this dimension would need to be chaotic in some way. And the concept of D-Class attacking 507 for no reason seems a bit odd. I doubt there would be any D-Class just roaming around the Foundation. Maybe 507 and the guard could've been friends, and the guard was patting him on the shoulder/had his hand on 507's shoulder when walking down the hall? Something like that may seem a bit more plausible. Here's the original text of Addendum 507-00 for reference

When questioned, it said that ████ was holding onto its shoulder when it shifted, leading to both of them to appear in an alternate dimension where [EXPUNGED]. During the ensuing chaos, SCP-507 lost contact with ████ and could not relocate him before it shifted back into “standard” reality.

*Are the villagers really doing anything about the Guard being there? I get they're behaviorally/physiologically different from humans, but I still feel they should have a bit more of a role in the story. Otherwise, I feel there's a bit of lost potential.


Aside from that, this is a perfect concept, and I can't wait to see the final article! Here's your greenlight, and please do reach out if you have any questions/comments/concerns.

item.title: Foundation 2.0
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Tragedy, Emotional, Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): A brief description and containment measures describing a parallel dimension which can be reached by some obscure ritual, and a village inside it, but story mainly told by a journal found by the foundation when they found out how to get inside. The foundation eventually leaves the dimension and doesn't return due to little reason to explore as the people and objects appear somewhat similar and they see no reason to take unnecessary risks.

Elevator Pitch: A foundation guard gets stuck in an alien dimension via contact with 507 when trying to break to break up a fight with a d class attacking them for some reason / the result of addemdum 507 - 00, and ends up in a parallel dimension with a village and villagers, that are similar to humans, but slightly behaviourally and physically different with a different language, and cause humans to disassociate from reality if continually touched

Central Narrative: The foundation later finds an obscure way into the dimension, and finds a journal and ruins of his base detailing his life. The agent steals from the villagers, and spies on them, trying to make proper files and dossiers on them, even making his own scp site, but eventually devolves into a cariacature of the foundation, capturing non - anomalous animals the he beleives are to study and make files on, as well as making overprecise and downright incorrect assumptions about the villagers in needless documents about their lives. He also tags the walls and trees with scp signs, and writes incoherent notes in his journal pertaining to enemies of the foundation and scps. He then breaks his leg and slowly dies because of sepsis, and reflects on what he did, and feels happy he contributed to the foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: How the guard loses his mind and becomes so obesessed with the foundation he forgets what it stands for and what it actually does, contain anomalies, and save humanity.

Additional Notes: I would like the journal to be somewhat comedic (eg: "gamers against weed are dumb little kids", "the goc is for nerds"), and make useless files on completely normal animals,
(e.g:
object class: keter
description: a rabbit i found, is anomalous but i dont know how yet
containment: a cage next to my bed
tests: eats carrots and shits occasionally), but I don't know if it would be funny enough/too meta/too much content

I'm new to this, so please correct me if anything stands out as off or out of place.
